# About this qmd

This qmd includes 2 parts:

1.  **Regions.** Maps of the outcomes and exposure with the four Census regions marked, and the main models (OLS M3 and SEM) run             separately in each region (Northeast, Midwest, South, West), all in one table.
2.  **The South.** descriptives and maps, unadjusted groupcomparisons, staged OLS models, and spatial error models (SEM andSDEM) with       model checks.

Data: it reads the same two files as the national notebook:

-   `data/final/national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.gpkg` from `processing_national_pumas_2022_2024.qmd`: outcomes, controls and
    PUMA boundaries
-   `data/final/puma_prison_exposure.csv` from processing_prison_exposure.qmd`: the prison exposure measures

Outcomes: `overdose_rate_2022_2024` (overdose deaths per 100,000, pooled 2022–2024 CDC tract data) and `pct_divorced_past_yr` (% of
ever-married people who divorced in the past year, pooled 2022–2024 ACS).

Exposure: distance-decay exposure to open state and federal prisons (h = 1, 5, 10 and 25 km), plus the number of prisons inside the PUMA and any prison inside the PUMA. The South is defined as the Census South region (16 states and DC).

# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(gt)
library(broom)
library(fixest)
library(spdep)
library(spatialreg)
library(tigris)
library(patchwork)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
set.seed(2024)
```

## Data

```{r}
#| label: data-load
# Exposure measures from processing_prison_exposure.qmd, outcomes and controls (with boundaries)
# from processing_national_pumas_2022_2024.qmd
exposure <- read_csv("data/final/puma_prison_exposure.csv",
                     col_types = cols(GEOID20 = col_character()))

# Census region for each state (base R state lists; DC added by hand)
state_regions <- tibble(state  = c(state.abb, "DC"),
                        region = c(as.character(state.region), "South")) %>%
  mutate(region = recode(region, "North Central" = "Midwest")) %>%
  left_join(distinct(tidycensus::fips_codes, state, state_code), by = "state") %>%
  select(state_fips = state_code, region)

puma_geo <- st_read("data/final/national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.gpkg", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  select(-any_of(setdiff(names(exposure), "GEOID20"))) %>%   # avoid .x/.y if the gpkg already has exposure columns
  left_join(exposure, by = "GEOID20") %>%
  left_join(state_regions, by = "state_fips") %>%
  mutate(rural = pct_pop_nonmetro > 50)                      # rural = more than half the population in non-metro tracts

puma_df <- puma_geo %>% st_drop_geometry()

nrow(puma_df)            # 2462
count(puma_df, region)   # PUMAs per region
count(puma_df, rural)    # rural vs. not

# Subsets: with boundaries (for maps and spatial models) and as plain tables
south_puma_geo       <- puma_geo %>% filter(region == "South")
south_rural_puma_geo <- puma_geo %>% filter(region == "South", rural)

south_puma_df       <- south_puma_geo       %>% st_drop_geometry()
south_rural_puma_df <- south_rural_puma_geo %>% st_drop_geometry()

tibble(sample = c("National", "South", "South rural"),
       PUMAs  = c(nrow(puma_df), 
                  nrow(south_puma_df), nrow(south_rural_puma_df)))

# Outcomes and their labels, used throughout
outcomes <- c(
  overdose_rate_2022_2024 = "Overdose deaths per 100,000",
  pct_divorced_past_yr    = "% of ever-married divorced in past year"
)

# Lower 48 for maps (Alaska and Hawaii would stretch the map); projected for correct shapes
puma_geo_l48 <- puma_geo %>%
  filter(!state_fips %in% c("02", "15")) %>%
  st_transform(5070)

# Open state and federal prisons, for plotting on the maps
prisons <- st_read("data/raw/prison-boundaries-1-geojson.geojson", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  filter(STATUS == "OPEN", TYPE %in% c("STATE", "FEDERAL")) %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  st_transform(5070) %>%
  st_filter(st_union(puma_geo_l48))
```

## Model setup (shared by both parts)

Exposure measures, controls and model specifications, the same as in the national notebook.

```{r}
#| label: model-setup
# Census division for each state (base R state lists; DC added by hand)
state_lookup <- tibble(state = state.abb,
                       division = as.character(state.division)) %>%
  add_row(state = "DC", division = "South Atlantic") %>%
  left_join(distinct(tidycensus::fips_codes, state, state_code), by = "state") %>%
  select(state_fips = state_code, division)

# Exposure measures: variable -> label
exposures <- c(
  prison_exp_h1          = "Exposure, h = 1 km",
  prison_exp_h5          = "Exposure, h = 5 km",
  prison_exp_h10         = "Exposure, h = 10 km",
  prison_exp_h25         = "Exposure, h = 25 km",
  num_prisons_in_puma    = "Number of prisons in PUMA",
  prison_present_in_puma = "Prison in PUMA (0/1)"
)

# Control groups
ctrl_geo  <- c("log_pop_density", "pct_pop_nonmetro", "log_pop")
ctrl_econ <- c("pct_unemployed", "log_medhhinc")
ctrl_educ <- c("pct_bachelors_plus")
ctrl_race <- c("pct_nonwhite")
ctrl_religion <-c("pct_religious")
ctrl_all  <- c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ, ctrl_educ, ctrl_race)
ctrl_all_div  <- c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ, ctrl_educ, ctrl_race, ctrl_religion)

# Model specifications: one row per stage, with its controls and fixed effects
specs_od <- tibble(
  spec     = c("M1", "M2", "M3a", "M3b", "M3c", "M3d", "M3", "M3-div"),
  controls = list(character(0), ctrl_geo, c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ), c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_educ),
                  c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_race), ctrl_all, ctrl_all, ctrl_all),
  fe       = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "state_fips", "division")
)

specs_div <- tibble(
  spec     = c("M1", "M2", "M3a", "M3b", "M3c", "M3d", "M3", "M3-div"),
  controls = list(character(0), ctrl_geo, c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_econ), c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_educ),
                  c(ctrl_geo, ctrl_race), ctrl_all_div, ctrl_all_div, ctrl_all_div),
  fe       = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "state_fips", "division")
)

# Both together, with the outcome each set of specs belongs to
specs <- bind_rows(
  specs_od  %>% mutate(y = "overdose_rate_2022_2024"),
  specs_div %>% mutate(y = "pct_divorced_past_yr")
)

weight_labels <- c(queen = "Queen", knn = "kNN (k = 6)")

# National model data: division added; continuous exposures standardized with the
# national mean and SD (used for the regional comparison)
puma_m <- puma_df %>%
  left_join(state_lookup, by = "state_fips") %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(setdiff(names(exposures), "prison_present_in_puma")),
                ~ (.x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

## Outcomes and exposure by region

```{r}
#| label: region-summary
puma_df %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(PUMAs              = n(),
            overdose_mean      = mean(overdose_rate_2022_2024, na.rm = TRUE),
            divorce_mean       = mean(pct_divorced_past_yr, na.rm = TRUE),
            exposure_h10_mean  = mean(prison_exp_h10, na.rm = TRUE),
            pct_with_prison    = 100 * mean(prison_present_in_puma, na.rm = TRUE),
            pct_nonmetro_pumas = 100 * mean(rural, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(overdose_mean, divorce_mean, exposure_h10_mean), decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(pct_with_prison, pct_nonmetro_pumas), decimals = 1) %>%
  cols_label(region = "Region", overdose_mean = "Overdose (mean)", divorce_mean = "Divorce (mean)",
             exposure_h10_mean = "Exposure h = 10 km (mean)",
             pct_with_prison = "% PUMAs with a prison", pct_nonmetro_pumas = "% non-metro PUMAs") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Outcomes and exposure by Census region")
```

## Models by region

The M3 specification (all controls + state fixed effects) run separately in each region, for every outcome and exposure: OLS with state-clustered SEs, and SEM with queen weights built within the region. Exposures are standardized nationally, so the β's can be compared across regions.

```{r}
#| label: region-setup
# One sample per region and outcome: complete cases for that outcome's M3 controls,
# with boundaries, queen weights and eigenvalues built within the region
region_data <- expand_grid(region = c("Northeast", "Midwest", "South", "West"),
                           y      = names(outcomes)) %>%
  left_join(specs %>% filter(spec == "M3") %>% select(y, controls), by = "y") %>%
  mutate(
    data = pmap(list(region, y, controls),
                ~ puma_m %>%
                    filter(region == ..1) %>%
                    drop_na(all_of(c(..2, names(exposures), ..3, "state_fips")))),
    # Same PUMAs with boundaries; the spatial models use this table so the rows match the weights
    geo  = map(data, ~ puma_geo %>%
                         select(GEOID20) %>%
                         st_transform(5070) %>%
                         inner_join(.x, by = "GEOID20")),
    lw   = map(geo, ~ nb2listw(poly2nb(.x, queen = TRUE, snap = 1), style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)),
    eig  = map(lw, ~ eigenw(similar.listw(.x))),
    n    = map_int(data, nrow)
  )

region_data %>% select(region, y, n)   # PUMAs per region and outcome

# Every region x outcome x exposure, with its M3 formula
region_models <- region_data %>%
  expand_grid(x = names(exposures)) %>%
  mutate(rhs         = map2_chr(x, controls, ~ str_c(c(.x, .y), collapse = " + ")),
         formula_ols = str_c(y, " ~ ", rhs, " | state_fips"),
         formula_sem = str_c(y, " ~ ", rhs, " + factor(state_fips)"))

# OLS M3 by region (fast, fitted every time)
region_ols <- region_models %>%
  mutate(model = map2(formula_ols, data, ~ feols(as.formula(.x), data = .y, cluster = ~state_fips)),
         coef  = map2(model, x, ~ tidy(.x) %>%
                                   filter(term == .y) %>%
                                   select(ols_beta = estimate, ols_p = p.value))) %>%
  select(region, y, x, coef) %>%
  unnest(coef)
```

```{r}
#| label: region-fit-sem
#| eval: false
# Run by hand once (4 regions x 2 outcomes x 6 exposures = 48 SEMs); saved and read below
region_models %>%
  mutate(sem = pmap(list(formula_sem, geo, lw, eig),
                    ~ errorsarlm(as.formula(..1), data = st_drop_geometry(..2),
                                 listw = ..3, method = "eigen",
                                 control = list(pre_eig = ..4), zero.policy = TRUE),
                    .progress = "SEM by region")) %>%
  select(region, y, x, sem) %>%
  saveRDS("data/final/region_sem_models.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: region-table
region_sem <- readRDS("data/final/region_sem_models.rds") %>%
  mutate(coef   = map2(sem, x, ~ as_tibble(summary(.x)$Coef, rownames = "term") %>%
                                  filter(term == .y) %>%
                                  transmute(sem_beta = Estimate, sem_p = `Pr(>|z|)`)),
         lambda = map_dbl(sem, ~ .x$lambda)) %>%
  select(region, y, x, coef, lambda) %>%
  unnest(coef)

region_results <- region_ols %>%
  left_join(region_sem, by = c("region", "y", "x")) %>%
  left_join(region_data %>% select(region, y, n), by = c("region", "y")) %>%
  mutate(outcome  = outcomes[y],
         exposure = factor(exposures[x], levels = exposures),
         region   = factor(region, levels = c("Northeast", "Midwest", "South", "West")))

region_results %>%
  select(outcome, exposure, region, n, ols_beta, ols_p, sem_beta, sem_p, lambda) %>%
  arrange(outcome, exposure, region) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("outcome", "exposure")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(ols_beta, sem_beta, lambda), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(ols_p, sem_p), decimals = 4) %>%
  cols_label(region = "Region", ols_beta = "OLS β", ols_p = "p",
             sem_beta = "SEM β", sem_p = "p", lambda = "λ") %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "OLS M3 (state-clustered SEs)", columns = c(ols_beta, ols_p)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "SEM (queen)", columns = c(sem_beta, sem_p, lambda)) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = sem_p < 0.05)) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Exposure coefficients by Census region (M3 specification)",
             subtitle = "Continuous exposures per national SD; presence = with vs. without. Shaded: SEM p < 0.05")
```

# THE SOUTH

Everything from here on uses only the Southern PUMAs.

## Descriptives

### Summary statistics

```{r}
#| label: summary-stats
summary_vars <- c(names(outcomes),
                  "prison_exp_h1", "prison_exp_h5", "prison_exp_h10", "prison_exp_h25",
                   "num_prisons_in_puma",
                  "pop_density", "pct_pop_rural", "pct_pop_nonmetro")

south_puma_df %>%
  select(all_of(summary_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(value)),
            mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE), median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = summary_vars)) %>%
  arrange(variable) %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean, sd, min, median, max), decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Summary statistics, PUMAs (2022–2024)")

table(south_puma_df$prison_present_in_puma, useNA = "ifany")   
```

#### Which PUMAs are selected as rural and as non-metro

A PUMA is selected when more than half of its population lives in that type of tract.

```{r}
#| label: map-rural-selection
south_geo %>%
  mutate(selected = if_else(pct_pop_nonmetro > 50, "Non-metro PUMA", "Not selected")) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = selected), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Non-metro PUMA" = "darkgreen", "Not selected" = "grey90"),
                    name = NULL, na.value = "grey85") +
  state_layer +
  labs(title = "South: PUMAs with more than 50% of the population in non-metro tracts",
       subtitle = "Non-metro = RUCA 4–10 (micropolitan, small town and rural)") +
  map_theme

south_geo %>%
  mutate(selected = if_else(pct_pop_rural > 50, "Rural PUMA", "Not selected")) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = selected), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Rural PUMA" = "darkorange3", "Not selected" = "grey90"),
                    name = NULL, na.value = "grey85") +
  state_layer +
  labs(title = "South: PUMAs with more than 50% of the population in rural tracts",
       subtitle = "Rural = RUCA 10 only") +
  map_theme
```

### Correlations

Spearman correlations, since most of the exposure measures are very skewed.

```{r}
#| label: correlations
cor_vars <- c(
  # Tract-based measures
  "Exposure h=1"             = "prison_exp_h1",
  "Exposure h=5"             = "prison_exp_h5",
  "Exposure h=10"             = "prison_exp_h10",
  "Exposure h=25"            = "prison_exp_h25",
  "Prisons in PUMA"           = "num_prisons_in_puma",
  "Prison in PUMA (0/1)"      = "prison_present_in_puma",
  # Settlement geography
  "Log density"               = "log_pop_density",
  "% rural (RUCA 10)"         = "pct_pop_rural",
  "% non-metro"               = "pct_pop_nonmetro"
)
cor_vars <- cor_vars[cor_vars %in% names(south_puma_df)]  

cor_mat <- south_puma_df %>%
  select(all_of(cor_vars)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")

# correlation matrix code
cor_long <- as_tibble(cor_mat, rownames = "var1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "rho") %>%
  mutate(var1 = factor(var1, levels = names(cor_vars)),
         var2 = factor(var2, levels = rev(names(cor_vars))))

ggplot(cor_long, aes(var1, var2, fill = rho)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", rho)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Spearman") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Correlations: exposure measures and settlement geography") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```

### Group comparisons

This section shows unadjusted comparisons of the outcomes across exposure groups. Prison presence gives two groups, and the number of prisons gives three (0, 1, 2+). Each decay measure is split into an "unexposed" group (exposure below 0.01, meaning no prison anywhere near where people live) and four equal-sized groups of the exposed PUMAs.

```{r}
#| label: groupings
south_puma_groups <- south_puma_df %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Any prison inside the PUMA
    grp_presence = factor(if_else(prison_present_in_puma == 1, "Prison in PUMA", "No prison"),
                          levels = c("No prison", "Prison in PUMA")),
    # 2. Number of prisons inside the PUMA
    grp_count = cut(num_prisons_in_puma, breaks = c(-Inf, 0, 1, Inf),
                    labels = c("0", "1", "2+")),
    # 3. Distance-decay exposure: "unexposed" (< 0.01), then quartiles of the exposed PUMAs
    grp_h1  = if_else(prison_exp_h1  < 0.01, "Unexposed",
                      paste0("Q", ntile(if_else(prison_exp_h1  >= 0.01, prison_exp_h1,  NA_real_), 4))),
    grp_h5  = if_else(prison_exp_h5  < 0.01, "Unexposed",
                      paste0("Q", ntile(if_else(prison_exp_h5  >= 0.01, prison_exp_h5,  NA_real_), 4))),
    grp_h10 = if_else(prison_exp_h10 < 0.01, "Unexposed",
                      paste0("Q", ntile(if_else(prison_exp_h10 >= 0.01, prison_exp_h10, NA_real_), 4))),
    grp_h25 = if_else(prison_exp_h25 < 0.01, "Unexposed",
                      paste0("Q", ntile(if_else(prison_exp_h25 >= 0.01, prison_exp_h25, NA_real_), 4))),
    across(c(grp_h1, grp_h5, grp_h10, grp_h25),
           ~ factor(.x, levels = c("Unexposed", "Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"))),
    # For the stratified comparison
    metro = factor(if_else(pct_pop_nonmetro > 50, "Non-metro PUMAs", "Metro PUMAs"))
  )

groupings <- c(
  grp_presence = "Prison inside the PUMA",
  grp_count    = "Number of prisons inside the PUMA",
  grp_h1       = "Decay exposure, h = 1 km",
  grp_h5       = "Decay exposure, h = 5 km",
  grp_h10      = "Decay exposure, h = 10 km",
  grp_h25      = "Decay exposure, h = 25 km"
)

# How many PUMAs in each group
south_puma_groups %>% count(grp_presence)
south_puma_groups %>% count(grp_count)
south_puma_groups %>% count(grp_h1)
south_puma_groups %>% count(grp_h5)
south_puma_groups %>% count(grp_h10)
south_puma_groups %>% count(grp_h25)
```

Mean, median and SD of each outcome in each group:

```{r}
#| label: group-means
# All group labels, in display order
group_levels <- c("No prison", "Prison in PUMA", "0", "1", "2+",
                  "Unexposed", "Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4")

# Long format: one row per PUMA x outcome x grouping
group_long <- south_puma_groups %>%
  select(GEOID20, all_of(names(outcomes)), all_of(names(groupings))) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(outcomes)), names_to = "y", values_to = "value") %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(groupings)), names_to = "g", values_to = "group",
               values_transform = as.character) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(group)) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = group_levels))

group_stats <- group_long %>%
  group_by(y, g, group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(value), median = median(value), sd = sd(value),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(outcome  = outcomes[y],
         grouping = factor(groupings[g], levels = groupings))

group_stats %>%
  select(outcome, grouping, group, n, mean, median, sd) %>%
  arrange(outcome, grouping, group) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("outcome", "grouping")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean, median, sd), decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Outcomes by prison exposure group")
```

The differences in means between groups show a similar pattern to the national dataset. However, the means, especially for overdose, seem to be higher in this case.

```{r}
#| label: group-tests
# Two groups (prison in PUMA vs not): Welch t-test and Wilcoxon rank-sum test
tests_presence <- group_long %>%
  filter(g == "grp_presence") %>%
  group_by(y, g) %>%
  summarise(
    test_means = "Welch t-test",
    difference = diff(t.test(value ~ droplevels(group))$estimate),   # prison minus no prison
    p_means    = t.test(value ~ droplevels(group))$p.value,
    test_ranks = "Wilcoxon",
    p_ranks    = wilcox.test(value ~ droplevels(group))$p.value,
    p_trend    = NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# More than two ordered groups (count and all decay measures):
# ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis and a linear trend test across the ordered groups
tests_ordered <- group_long %>%
  filter(g != "grp_presence") %>%
  group_by(y, g) %>%
  summarise(
    test_means = "ANOVA",
    difference = NA_real_,
    p_means    = anova(lm(value ~ droplevels(group)))$`Pr(>F)`[1],
    test_ranks = "Kruskal-Wallis",
    p_ranks    = kruskal.test(value ~ droplevels(group))$p.value,
    p_trend    = tidy(lm(value ~ as.integer(droplevels(group))))$p.value[2],   # groups as 1, 2, 3, ...
    .groups = "drop"
  )

test_results <- bind_rows(tests_presence, tests_ordered) %>%
  mutate(outcome  = outcomes[y],
         grouping = factor(groupings[g], levels = groupings)) %>%
  arrange(outcome, grouping) %>%
  select(outcome, grouping, test_means, difference, p_means, test_ranks, p_ranks, p_trend)

test_results %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "outcome") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = difference, decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(p_means, p_ranks, p_trend), decimals = 4) %>%
  sub_missing(missing_text = "") %>%
  cols_label(grouping = "Grouping", test_means = "Means test", difference = "Difference",
             p_means = "p (means)", test_ranks = "Rank test", p_ranks = "p (ranks)",
             p_trend = "p (linear trend)") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Do outcomes differ by prison exposure? (unadjusted)",
subtitle = "Difference = with prison minus without (two-group comparisons only)")
```

These tests check whether the outcomes differ across groups. For the two-group comparison (prison vs. no prison), we used a Welch t-test for the means and a Wilcoxon rank-sum test for the whole distributions. For the groupings with more than two groups, we used ANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis, plus a linear trend test across the ordered groups. These tests ignore the controls and assume that PUMAs are independent (they are not), so they are descriptive only.

#### Within metro and non-metro PUMAs

The same prison vs. no prison comparison, separately for metro and non-metro PUMAs.

```{r}
#| label: group-stratified
# Prison vs. no prison, separately in metro and non-metro PUMAs.
# Welch t-test (means) and Wilcoxon rank-sum test (distributions), as in the main comparison.
stratified <- south_puma_groups %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(outcomes)), names_to = "y", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(grp_presence)) %>%
  group_by(y, metro) %>%
  summarise(
    n_no_prison    = sum(grp_presence == "No prison"),
    n_prison       = sum(grp_presence == "Prison in PUMA"),
    mean_no_prison = t.test(value ~ grp_presence)$estimate[[1]],
    mean_prison    = t.test(value ~ grp_presence)$estimate[[2]],
    difference     = mean_prison - mean_no_prison,              # prison minus no prison
    p_means        = t.test(value ~ grp_presence)$p.value,
    p_ranks        = wilcox.test(value ~ grp_presence)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(outcome = outcomes[y])

stratified %>%
  select(outcome, metro, n_no_prison, n_prison, mean_no_prison, mean_prison,
         difference, p_means, p_ranks) %>%
  arrange(outcome, metro) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "outcome") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean_no_prison, mean_prison, difference), decimals = 2) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(p_means, p_ranks), decimals = 4) %>%
  cols_label(metro = "PUMAs", n_no_prison = "n (no prison)", n_prison = "n (prison)",
             mean_no_prison = "Mean (no prison)", mean_prison = "Mean (prison)",
             difference = "Difference", p_means = "p (t-test)", p_ranks = "p (Wilcoxon)") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Prison vs. no prison, within metro and non-metro PUMAs (unadjusted)")
```

Again, the pattern from the national dataset holds: rural pumas with prisons have lower means for both overdose and divorce...:(

## Staged OLS models

Each model has one exposure measure. Controls are added in stages so we can see how much the exposure coefficient moves at each step.

| Model | Adds |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| M1 | nothing (exposure only) |
| M2 | settlement geography: log density, % non-metro, log population |
| M3a | M2 + economic: % unemployed, log median income |
| M3b | M2 + education: % bachelor's or more |
| M3c | M2 + race: % non-White |
| M3d | M2 + all of the above |
| M3 | M3d + state fixed effects (main adjusted model) |
| M3-div | M3d + Census division fixed effects |

### Setup and fitting

```{r}
#| label: p4-setup
# Model data: add division and log distance; standardize continuous exposures
south_puma_m <- south_puma_df %>%
  left_join(state_lookup, by = "state_fips") %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(setdiff(names(exposures), "prison_present_in_puma")),
                ~ (.x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))

# One complete-case sample per outcome, using that outcome's own full control set
# (same PUMAs in every model for that outcome)
south_model_data <- list(
  overdose_rate_2022_2024 = south_puma_m %>%
    drop_na(all_of(c("overdose_rate_2022_2024", names(exposures), ctrl_all,
                     "state_fips", "division"))),
  pct_divorced_past_yr = south_puma_m %>%
    drop_na(all_of(c("pct_divorced_past_yr", names(exposures), ctrl_all_div,
                     "state_fips", "division")))
)

map_int(south_model_data, nrow)   # PUMAs per outcome
```

```{r}
#| label: p4-fit
# Every outcome x specification (its own specs) x exposure, with its formula written out
south_all_models <- specs %>%
  expand_grid(x = names(exposures)) %>%
  mutate(
    rhs     = map2_chr(x, controls, ~ str_c(c(.x, .y), collapse = " + ")),
    formula = str_c(y, " ~ ", rhs, if_else(is.na(fe), "", str_c(" | ", fe))),
    model   = map2(formula, y, ~ feols(as.formula(.x), data = south_model_data[[.y]],
                                       cluster = ~state_fips))
  )

south_all_models %>% distinct(y, spec, formula)   # check: the divorce M3d/M3/M3-div should include the extra controls

# Pull out the exposure coefficient from each model
results <- south_all_models %>%
  mutate(
    coef = map2(model, x, ~ tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
                              filter(term == .y) %>%
                              select(estimate, std.error, p.value, conf.low, conf.high)),
    r2 = map_dbl(model, ~ r2(.x, "r2")),
    n  = map_int(model, nobs)
  ) %>%
  select(y, x, spec, coef, r2, n) %>%
  unnest(coef) %>%
    mutate(spec = factor(spec, levels = specs_od$spec)) %>%
  group_by(y, x) %>%
  arrange(spec, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(pct_change_from_M1 = 100 * (estimate - first(estimate)) / abs(first(estimate))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(outcome  = outcomes[y],
         exposure = factor(exposures[x], levels = exposures))
```

## Spatial models

| Model | Assumes | Role here |
|-----------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------|
| SEM | nearby PUMAs share unmeasured conditions, so their errors are correlated | main spatial model |
| SDEM | SEM + exposure in neighboring PUMAs can matter too | do prisons just outside a PUMA matter? |

Both keep the full M3 specification (each outcome with its own controls). They're estimated by maximum likelihood, so the standard errors are model-based, not clustered.

### Setup

Neighbors are defined only within the South, so PUMAs on the edge of the region have fewer neighbors than in the national data. The spatial models need neighbor relations to go both ways, so the kNN weights were made symmetric: two PUMAs are neighbors if either one is among the other's 6 nearest. Because of this, some PUMAs end up with a few morevthan six neighbors.

```{r}
#| label: south-spatial-setup
# Southern model data with boundaries, one per outcome (same PUMAs as the South OLS models).
# Rows stay in this order for the models and the weights.
south_geo_data <- map(names(outcomes),
                      ~ puma_geo %>%
                          select(GEOID20) %>%
                          st_transform(5070) %>%
                          inner_join(south_model_data[[.x]], by = "GEOID20")) %>%
  set_names(names(outcomes))

# Neighbors within the South only
south_queen_nb <- map(south_geo_data, ~ poly2nb(.x, queen = TRUE, snap = 1))
south_knn_nb   <- map(south_geo_data, ~ .x %>%
                                          st_geometry() %>%
                                          st_point_on_surface() %>%
                                          st_coordinates() %>%
                                          knearneigh(k = 6) %>%
                                          knn2nb())

weight_labels <- c(queen = "Queen", knn = "kNN (k = 6)")

# Weights for the spatial models (kNN made symmetric for the eigen method)
south_p6_weights <- map2(south_queen_nb, south_knn_nb,
                         ~ list(queen = nb2listw(.x, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE),
                                knn   = nb2listw(make.sym.nb(.y), style = "W")))

# Eigenvalues, computed once
south_p6_eig <- map(south_p6_weights, ~ list(queen = eigenw(similar.listw(.x$queen)),
                                             knn   = eigenw(similar.listw(.x$knn))))

# PUMAs with no queen neighbor inside the South (e.g. on the region's edge or islands)
map_int(south_queen_nb, ~ sum(card(.x) == 0))
```

```{r}
#| label: south-spatial-formulas
# South M3 formulas for each outcome and exposure, written with state dummies
# (spatial models can't use feols's "| state_fips" fixed-effects syntax)
south_spatial_models <- south_all_models %>%
  filter(spec == "M3") %>%
  transmute(y, x,
            formula_lm = str_replace(formula, " \\| state_fips", " + factor(state_fips)"))
```

```{r}
#| label: south-load-error-models
south_error_models <- readRDS("data/final/south_error_models.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: p6-extract-error-models
south_error_results <- south_error_models %>%
  mutate(
    # SEM: the exposure coefficient
    sem_coef = map2(sem, x, ~ as_tibble(summary(.x)$Coef, rownames = "term") %>%
                               filter(term == .y) %>%
                               transmute(estimate = Estimate, std.error = `Std. Error`,
                                         p.value = `Pr(>|z|)`)),
    sem_lambda = map_dbl(sem, ~ .x$lambda),
    sem_aic    = map_dbl(sem, AIC),

    # SDEM direct: exposure in the PUMA itself
    sdem_direct = map2(sdem, x, ~ as_tibble(summary(.x)$Coef, rownames = "term") %>%
                                   filter(term == .y) %>%
                                   transmute(estimate = Estimate, std.error = `Std. Error`,
                                             p.value = `Pr(>|z|)`)),
    # SDEM indirect: exposure in neighboring PUMAs (the "lag." term)
    sdem_indirect = map2(sdem, x, ~ as_tibble(summary(.x)$Coef, rownames = "term") %>%
                                     filter(term == paste0("lag.", .y)) %>%
                                     transmute(estimate = Estimate, std.error = `Std. Error`,
                                               p.value = `Pr(>|z|)`)),
    # SDEM total = direct + indirect; its SE uses the covariance between the two
    sdem_total = map2(sdem, x, ~ tibble(
                   estimate  = sum(coef(.x)[c(.y, paste0("lag.", .y))]),
                   std.error = sqrt(sum(vcov(.x)[c(.y, paste0("lag.", .y)),
                                                 c(.y, paste0("lag.", .y))]))) %>%
                   mutate(p.value = 2 * pnorm(-abs(estimate / std.error)))),
    sdem_lambda = map_dbl(sdem, ~ .x$lambda),
    sdem_aic    = map_dbl(sdem, AIC)
  ) %>%
  select(-sem, -sdem)

# OLS M3 (state-clustered) from Phase 4, for comparison
ols_m3 <- results %>%
  filter(spec == "M3") %>%
  select(y, x, ols_estimate = estimate, ols_se = std.error, ols_p = p.value)
```

### One exposure in detail: OLS vs. SEM vs. SDEM

Set `main_x` at the top of the chunk to choose the exposure. It is also used by the model checks below.

```{r}
#| label: p6-main-table
# One comparison table: OLS M3 vs. SEM vs. SDEM for the main exposure,
# for each outcome and weights matrix

# specify the variable you want to look at
#options: prison_exp_h1, prison_exp_h5, prison_exp_h10, prison_exp_h25, num_prisons_in_puma, prison_present_in_puma
main_x <- "prison_exp_h1"

main_table <- bind_rows(
  # OLS M3 doesn't use the weights, so the same row is repeated for both weights matrices
  ols_m3 %>%
    filter(x == main_x) %>%
    expand_grid(w = names(weight_labels)) %>%
    transmute(y, w, model = "OLS M3 (state-clustered SEs)", effect = "Coefficient",
              estimate = ols_estimate, std.error = ols_se, p.value = ols_p,
              spatial_param = NA_real_, aic = NA_real_),

  # SEM: exposure coefficient, with lambda and AIC
  south_error_results %>%
    filter(x == main_x) %>%
    select(y, w, sem_coef, sem_lambda, sem_aic) %>%
    unnest(sem_coef) %>%
    transmute(y, w, model = "SEM", effect = "Coefficient",
              estimate, std.error, p.value,
              spatial_param = sem_lambda, aic = sem_aic),

  # SDEM direct: exposure in the PUMA itself (lambda and AIC shown on this row)
  south_error_results %>%
    filter(x == main_x) %>%
    select(y, w, sdem_direct, sdem_lambda, sdem_aic) %>%
    unnest(sdem_direct) %>%
    transmute(y, w, model = "SDEM", effect = "Direct",
              estimate, std.error, p.value,
              spatial_param = sdem_lambda, aic = sdem_aic),

  # SDEM indirect: exposure in neighboring PUMAs
  south_error_results %>%
    filter(x == main_x) %>%
    select(y, w, sdem_indirect) %>%
    unnest(sdem_indirect) %>%
    transmute(y, w, model = "SDEM", effect = "Indirect (neighbors)",
              estimate, std.error, p.value,
              spatial_param = NA_real_, aic = NA_real_),

  # SDEM total: direct + indirect
  south_error_results %>%
    filter(x == main_x) %>%
    select(y, w, sdem_total) %>%
    unnest(sdem_total) %>%
    transmute(y, w, model = "SDEM", effect = "Total",
              estimate, std.error, p.value,
              spatial_param = NA_real_, aic = NA_real_)
) %>%
  mutate(outcome = outcomes[y],
         weights = weight_labels[w],
         model   = factor(model, levels = c("OLS M3 (state-clustered SEs)", "SEM", "SDEM")),
         effect  = factor(effect, levels = c("Coefficient", "Direct",
                                             "Indirect (neighbors)", "Total"))) %>%
  arrange(outcome, weights, model, effect)

main_table %>%
  select(outcome, weights, model, effect, estimate, std.error, p.value, spatial_param, aic) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("outcome", "weights")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std.error, spatial_param), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = aic, decimals = 1) %>%
  sub_missing(missing_text = "") %>%
  cols_label(model = "Model", effect = "Effect", estimate = "β", std.error = "SE",
             p.value = "p", spatial_param = "λ", aic = "AIC") %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = p.value < 0.05)) %>%
  tab_header(title = paste0("Main exposure (", exposures[[main_x]], ", per SD): OLS vs. spatial error models"),
             subtitle = "λ = spatial error parameter (how strongly neighboring PUMAs share unexplained variation). Shaded: p < 0.05")
```


### All exposure measures: OLS vs. SEM vs. SDEM

```{r}
#| label: p6-all-table
south_error_results %>%
  mutate(sem = sem_coef, direct = sdem_direct, indirect = sdem_indirect) %>%
  select(y, x, w, sem, direct, indirect, sem_lambda) %>%
  unnest_wider(sem,      names_sep = "_") %>%
  unnest_wider(direct,   names_sep = "_") %>%
  unnest_wider(indirect, names_sep = "_") %>%
  left_join(ols_m3, by = c("y", "x")) %>%
  mutate(outcome  = outcomes[y],
         exposure = factor(exposures[x], levels = exposures),
         weights  = weight_labels[w]) %>%
  arrange(outcome, weights, exposure) %>%
  select(outcome, weights, exposure,
         ols_estimate, ols_p,
         sem_estimate, sem_p.value,
         direct_estimate, direct_p.value,
         indirect_estimate, indirect_p.value,
         sem_lambda) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = c("outcome", "weights")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(ols_estimate, sem_estimate, direct_estimate, indirect_estimate, sem_lambda),
             decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(ols_p, sem_p.value, direct_p.value, indirect_p.value), decimals = 4) %>%
  cols_label(exposure = "Exposure", ols_estimate = "OLS β", ols_p = "p",
             sem_estimate = "SEM β", sem_p.value = "p",
             direct_estimate = "SDEM direct", direct_p.value = "p",
             indirect_estimate = "SDEM indirect", indirect_p.value = "p",
             sem_lambda = "SEM λ") %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "OLS M3", columns = c(ols_estimate, ols_p)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "SEM", columns = c(sem_estimate, sem_p.value, sem_lambda)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "SDEM", columns = c(direct_estimate, direct_p.value,
                                          indirect_estimate, indirect_p.value)) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Exposure coefficients: OLS M3 vs. spatial error models",
             subtitle = "Continuous exposures per SD; presence = with vs. without")
```


### Model checks

Three checks for the exposure chosen in `main_x`: a Hausman test (do the OLS and SEM coefficients differ more than chance allows?), Moran's I on the SEM and SDEM residuals (should be close to zero), and AIC for OLS
M3, SEM and SDEM (lower is better).

```{r}
#| label: p6-checks
# Hausman test: do OLS and SEM coefficients differ more than chance allows?
hausman_safe <- possibly(Hausman.test, otherwise = list(statistic = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_))

hausman <- south_error_models %>%
  filter(x == main_x) %>%
  mutate(test      = map(sem, hausman_safe),
         statistic = map_dbl(test, ~ unname(.x$statistic)),
         p.value   = map_dbl(test, ~ .x$p.value)) %>%
  transmute(outcome = outcomes[y], weights = weight_labels[w], statistic, p.value)
hausman

# Is spatial structure left in the residuals of SEM and SDEM? (Should be close to zero)
resid_moran <- south_error_models %>%
  filter(x == main_x) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(sem, sdem), names_to = "model", values_to = "fit") %>%
  mutate(
    lw = map2(y, w, ~ south_p6_weights[[.x]][[.y]]),
    e  = map(fit, ~ as.vector(.x$y - .x$X %*% .x$coefficients)),
    u  = pmap(list(e, fit, lw), ~ ..1 - ..2$lambda * lag.listw(..3, ..1, zero.policy = TRUE)),
    moran_I = map2_dbl(u, lw, ~ unname(moran.test(.x, .y, zero.policy = TRUE)$estimate[1])),
    moran_p = map2_dbl(u, lw, ~ moran.test(.x, .y, zero.policy = TRUE)$p.value)
  ) %>%
  transmute(outcome = outcomes[y], weights = weight_labels[w],
            model = toupper(model), moran_I, moran_p)
resid_moran

# Fit across models for the main measure (lower AIC = better).
south_error_results %>%
  filter(x == main_x) %>%
  select(y, w, sem_aic, sdem_aic) %>%
  left_join(south_spatial_models %>%
              filter(x == main_x) %>%
              mutate(ols = map2(formula_lm, y,
                                ~ lm(as.formula(.x), data = st_drop_geometry(south_geo_data[[.y]]))),
                     ols_aic = map_dbl(ols, AIC)) %>%
              select(y, ols_aic),
            by = "y") %>%
  mutate(outcome = outcomes[y], weights = weight_labels[w]) %>%
  select(outcome, weights, `OLS M3` = ols_aic, SEM = sem_aic, SDEM = sdem_aic)
```
